There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible
answers A, B, C and D.
Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet.
Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully.
Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer.
Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
This document consists of 10 printed pages and 2 blank pages.

At 1 January 2014 a business had prepaid rent of $700. In July it paid an invoice for $9300 and
on 31 December it transferred an expense of $9000 to the income statement.
Which value appeared in the statement of financial position at 31 December 2014?
Which cost should be treated as revenue expenditure?
A installing a new sound system in a car
B purchase of a trailer for a car
C replacing a damaged engine of a car
D replacing an old car with a new one
A sales return of $400 has been credited to the customer’s account as $40.
A suspense account is created to complete the trial balance.
What is the balance on the suspense account?
The creation of a provision for doubtful debts is an example of which accounting concept?
A business provided the following information.
30 April credit purchases for the month 42653
30 April payments made to trade payables 37324
What is the balance on the purchases ledger control account at 30 April?
A business depreciates its motor vehicles over four years using the straight-line method. A full
year’s depreciation is charged in the year of purchase, but none in the year of sale.
A vehicle purchased on 1 July 2011 for $18000 had an estimated residual value of $4000. The
vehicle was sold for $5000 on 31 December 2014.
Which entry appeared in the income statement for the year ended 31 December 2014?
Rachel’s trial balance did not agree and she placed the difference in a suspense account.
The following shows how four errors have been corrected using the suspense account.
difference in trial balance 200 discount received 310
The profit for the year before the errors were corrected was $35400.
What is the correct profit for the year?
A bank reconciliation statement has been prepared by an inexperienced book-keeper.
cheques paid to suppliers, not yet presented (41800)
What is the correct bank balance according to the cash book?
An invoice for purchases was credited to the purchases account.
How is the balance on the purchases account corrected?
A decrease by the value of the invoice
B decrease by twice the value of the invoice
C increase by the value of the invoice
D increase by twice the value of the invoice
Which item may appear in the manufacturing account of a business?
Inventory is valued at the lower of cost and net realisable value.
B selling price less cash discount
C selling price less further cost to completion
D selling price less trade discount
A trader runs a manufacturing business.
A department 1 where contribution exceeds fixed costs
B department 2 where contribution is less than fixed costs
C department 3 where revenue exceeds marginal costs
D department 4 where revenue is less than marginal costs
A club provides the following information.
How much are subscriptions for the year in the income and expenditure account?

A 1 and 2 B 1 and 3 C 2 and 3 D 2 and 4
When is working capital most likely to increase?
A when the business increases its selling prices
B when the credit period allowed to customers is reduced
C when the credit period taken from suppliers is increased
D when the value of inventory decreases
John failed to write off a bad debt of $8000.
What was the effect of this omission?
A His trade payables turnover (in days) was overstated.
B His trade payables turnover (in days) was understated.
C His trade receivables turnover (in days) was overstated.
D His trade receivables turnover (in days) was understated.
A customer places an order for 20 000 bricks.
Which costing method will the supplier use to price the order?
Which item is classed as a direct cost?
A business sells its product for $50 a unit and has variable costs of $30 per unit. Its fixed costs for
this year were $200000. Next year, fixed costs are expected to be $260000.
How many more units will have to be sold next year to make the same profit as this year?
A manufacturer produces 100000 tins of paint with a total direct materials cost of $300000.
Direct labour is 2000 hours at a cost of $400000, and overheads are absorbed at the rate of $100
What is the cost of a tin of paint?
A business provides the following information.
The variable overhead rate per machine hour was $8.
What was the monthly fixed cost?
A business produces a single product.
The variable production cost per unit is $10 and the fixed production cost is $60000. The sales
Profit is $108 000 based on full absorption costing.
What is the profit based on marginal costing?

What is the overhead absorption rate for the cost centre?
